title.en: History: Intellectual Awakening and Socio-Political Changes

text.en: Asha heard that Buddha and Mahavira lived about the same time. "Why so many thinkers then?" she asked.

Around the sixth century BCE new ideas arose in India. Jainism, taught by Mahavira, stresses non-violence, truth and non-possession. Buddhism, taught by Gautama Buddha, speaks of the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path to end suffering.
The same time saw thinkers elsewhere: Confucius in China, Socrates and Plato in Greece and Zoroaster in Persia. Kingdoms called Mahajanapadas grew in north India, and Magadha rose to power.
Ashoka the Maurya spread Buddhism and the message of dhamma after the Kalinga war. Tamil culture had its own thought, and the Thirukkural, with its teachings on virtue, wealth and love, came to be treasured.

problem.en: Why did Ashoka turn to dhamma?

text.en: The Kalinga war caused great suffering.

prompt.en: A friend says Buddha taught about the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path in Greece. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: The Four Noble Truths are Buddhist.

points.en: New religions arose in the 6th century BCE.
